records: Requests are made to BT, or to KCOM in the Hull area.
An applicant does not need to be an existing BT or KCOM customer.
BT or KCOM has 30 days to confirm eligibility and estimated build cost.
Eligibility requires no access to an existing decent broadband service.
Eligibility also requires that no public broadband scheme is due to cover the premises within 12 months.
A customer whose only decent service costs more than £59.60 per month can request a universal-service connection.
A network build or upgrade costing £3,400 or less for the applicant's share is provided without a construction charge.
If construction costs exceed £3,400, an applicant who proceeds must pay the excess.
For an above-threshold build, BT or KCOM conducts a survey and supplies a quote within 60 days.
The resulting service must cost no more than £59.60 per month.
Most eligible applicants are expected to receive a connection within 12 months.
Some universal-service connections can take up to 24 months.
An ineligible applicant may be offered satellite broadband, which requires a satellite dish.
BT or KCOM must explain the right to challenge an ineligibility decision and how to complain.
Customers have free access to ADR after eight unresolved weeks or sooner after deadlock.
Ofcom's General Conditions of Entitlement page was published on 16 August 2023.
The General Conditions page was last updated on 8 April 2026.
All providers of electronic communications networks and services must comply with applicable General Conditions to provide UK services.
The General Conditions replaced the Telecommunications Act 1984 licensing regime on 25 July 2003.
General Conditions are generally applicable and are not imposed on named individual providers.
The current consolidated General Conditions came into force on 8 April 2026.
The General Conditions are grouped into network functioning, numbering and technical, and consumer protection categories.
Condition A1 requires public network providers to negotiate interconnection agreements on request.
Condition A3 requires free access to emergency organisations and caller-location information where technically feasible.
Condition C1 requires a fixed-broadband contract to include a short description of the underlying technology.
Ofcom's Comparing Customer Service page was last updated on 25 May 2026.
The current Comparing Customer Service publication is Ofcom's eighth report in the series.
The report covers residential telecoms customer-service experiences in 2024.
Ofcom moved the Comparing Customer Service report to biennial publication after the 2023 report.
Ofcom flagged certain EE broadband and landline faults data and associated industry averages as subject to restatement after an April 2026 resubmission.
